# Support Vector Machines (SVM)

::: {.callout-note title="Connection with the theoretical volume"}
The mathematical treatment of **margins, convex optimization, KKT conditions, and kernels** is developed in greater depth in Chapters 4 and 15 of *Mathematical Foundations of Machine Learning* [@rodriguez2026fundamentos].
:::

## Learning objectives

By the end of this chapter, the reader will be able to:

- explain separating hyperplanes and maximum-margin classification;
- identify support vectors;
- distinguish hard- and soft-margin classification;
- compare linear and radial-kernel SVMs;
- interpret the roles of `cost`, `gamma`, scaling, and class weights;
- select the kernel and hyperparameters using validation without looking at the final test set;
- evaluate SVMs using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1, and balanced accuracy;
- apply SVMs to ATUS and to an educational COVID-19 route.

## Geometric intuition

For two predictors, a linear decision boundary can be written as

$$
w_1x_1+w_2x_2+b=0.
$$

In the ideally separable case, the constraints are

$$
y_i(\mathbf{w}^{T}\mathbf{x}_i+b)\geq 1,
$$

with $y_i\in\{-1,1\}$. The margin width is proportional to

$$
\frac{2}{\lVert\mathbf{w}\rVert}.
$$

Observations on or inside the margins directly determine the solution and are called **support vectors** [@cortes1995support; @burges1998tutorial].

::: {.callout-tip title="Essential idea"}
An SVM does not simply try to maximize training accuracy. It balances separation and violations in order to construct a boundary that can generalize to new observations.
:::

## Soft margin and `cost`

Real data are rarely perfectly separable. The soft-margin SVM allows violations through slack variables $\xi_i$ and solves, schematically,

$$
\min_{\mathbf{w},b,\xi}
\frac{1}{2}\lVert\mathbf{w}\rVert^2+C\sum_i\xi_i.
$$

The `cost` parameter corresponds to $C$:

- smaller values tolerate more violations and favor a wider margin;
- larger values penalize violations more strongly and may fit training data more closely.

There is no universally best `cost`; it must be selected with validation.

## Kernels

When a linear boundary is insufficient, an SVM can use a kernel. The radial basis function kernel is

$$
K(\mathbf{x}_i,\mathbf{x}_j)=
\exp\left(-\gamma\lVert\mathbf{x}_i-\mathbf{x}_j\rVert^2\right).
$$

The parameter $\gamma$ controls the local influence of each observation:

- small values produce smoother boundaries;
- larger values allow more local and complex boundaries.

::: {.callout-warning title="Complexity and overfitting"}
A large combination of `cost` and `gamma` can fit training data extremely well and generalize poorly. Both hyperparameters must be selected without looking at the final test set.
:::

## Geometric example with simulated data

```{r svm-simulated-data-en}
set.seed(123)

n <- 120

svm_data <- data.frame(
  x1 = c(
    rnorm(n / 2, mean = -1.5, sd = 0.8),
    rnorm(n / 2, mean =  1.5, sd = 0.8)
  ),
  x2 = c(
    rnorm(n / 2, mean = -1.0, sd = 0.9),
    rnorm(n / 2, mean =  1.0, sd = 0.9)
  ),
  class = factor(rep(c("Class A", "Class B"), each = n / 2))
)
```

```{r svm-simulated-plot-en, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
library(ggplot2)
source("../util_graficas.R")

ggplot(svm_data, aes(x = x1, y = x2, color = class)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5, alpha = 0.8) +
  labs(
    title = "Simulated data for SVM classification",
    x = "x1",
    y = "x2",
    color = "Class"
  ) +
  tema_libro()
```

## Fit a linear SVM and identify support vectors

```{r svm-linear-simulated-en}
library(e1071)

model_svm_linear <- svm(
  class ~ x1 + x2,
  data = svm_data,
  kernel = "linear",
  cost = 1,
  scale = TRUE
)

support_indices <- model_svm_linear$index
support_vectors <- svm_data[support_indices, ]

model_svm_linear$tot.nSV
```

```{r svm-linear-boundary-en, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
grid <- expand.grid(
  x1 = seq(min(svm_data$x1) - 0.5,
           max(svm_data$x1) + 0.5,
           length.out = 180),
  x2 = seq(min(svm_data$x2) - 0.5,
           max(svm_data$x2) + 0.5,
           length.out = 180)
)

grid$prediction <- predict(model_svm_linear, newdata = grid)

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(
    data = grid,
    aes(x = x1, y = x2, fill = prediction),
    alpha = 0.18
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = svm_data,
    aes(x = x1, y = x2, color = class),
    size = 2.2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = support_vectors,
    aes(x = x1, y = x2),
    shape = 21,
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.1,
    fill = NA
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Linear SVM decision boundary",
    subtitle = "Large circles mark support vectors",
    x = "x1",
    y = "x2",
    fill = "Prediction",
    color = "Actual class"
  ) +
  tema_libro()
```

## Scaling without information leakage

SVMs are sensitive to predictor scale. With `e1071::svm()`, `scale = TRUE` estimates centering and scaling parameters **from the data used to fit the model** and stores them for later predictions.

::: {.callout-important title="Correct order"}
First split the data into training, validation, and test sets. Then fit each SVM with `scale = TRUE`. Do not standardize the complete dataset before splitting.
:::

## Helper functions

```{r svm-helper-functions-en}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

stratified_svm_split <- function(
  y,
  prop_train = 0.60,
  prop_val = 0.20,
  seed = 2026
) {
  set.seed(seed)
  y <- factor(y)

  idx_train <- integer(0)
  idx_val <- integer(0)
  idx_test <- integer(0)

  for (class_value in levels(y)) {
    ids <- sample(which(y == class_value))
    n_train <- floor(prop_train * length(ids))
    n_val <- floor(prop_val * length(ids))

    ids_train <- ids[seq_len(n_train)]
    remaining <- ids[-seq_len(n_train)]
    ids_val <- remaining[seq_len(n_val)]
    ids_test <- setdiff(remaining, ids_val)

    idx_train <- c(idx_train, ids_train)
    idx_val <- c(idx_val, ids_val)
    idx_test <- c(idx_test, ids_test)
  }

  list(
    train = sort(idx_train),
    validation = sort(idx_val),
    test = sort(idx_test)
  )
}

svm_metrics <- function(actual, predicted, positive, negative) {
  actual <- factor(actual, levels = c(negative, positive))
  predicted <- factor(predicted, levels = c(negative, positive))
  m <- table(Actual = actual, Predicted = predicted)

  TP <- m[positive, positive]
  FN <- m[positive, negative]
  FP <- m[negative, positive]
  TN <- m[negative, negative]

  safe_divide <- function(a, b) if (b == 0) NA_real_ else as.numeric(a / b)

  sensitivity <- safe_divide(TP, TP + FN)
  specificity <- safe_divide(TN, TN + FP)
  precision <- safe_divide(TP, TP + FP)
  f1 <- if (
    is.na(precision) || is.na(sensitivity) ||
    precision + sensitivity == 0
  ) {
    NA_real_
  } else {
    2 * precision * sensitivity / (precision + sensitivity)
  }

  list(
    confusion = m,
    metrics = data.frame(
      accuracy = safe_divide(TP + TN, sum(m)),
      sensitivity = sensitivity,
      specificity = specificity,
      precision = precision,
      f1 = f1,
      balanced_accuracy = mean(c(sensitivity, specificity), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )
}
```

# Applied Case A: ATUS

## Load and prepare a reproducible sample

```{r svm-prepare-atus-en}
atus_path <- "../datos/atus_ml_preparado.csv"

if (!file.exists(atus_path)) {
  stop("../datos/atus_ml_preparado.csv was not found. Run Chapter 2 first.")
}

atus_ml <- read_csv(atus_path, show_col_types = FALSE)

set.seed(2026)
atus_svm <- atus_ml |>
  mutate(
    accident_class = factor(
      accidente_con_victimas,
      levels = c("Solo daños", "Con víctimas"),
      labels = c("Property damage only", "With casualties")
    ),
    MES = factor(MES),
    HOUR_NUM = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(ID_HORA)),
    HOUR_NUM = ifelse(
      HOUR_NUM >= 0 & HOUR_NUM <= 23,
      HOUR_NUM,
      NA_real_
    ),
    DIASEMANA = factor(DIASEMANA),
    TIPACCID = factor(TIPACCID),
    CAUSAACCI = factor(CAUSAACCI)
  ) |>
  drop_na(
    accident_class,
    MES,
    HOUR_NUM,
    DIASEMANA,
    TIPACCID,
    CAUSAACCI
  ) |>
  slice_sample(n = min(6000, n()))

prop.table(table(atus_svm$accident_class))
```

## Training, validation, and test sets

```{r svm-split-atus-en}
parts_atus <- stratified_svm_split(
  atus_svm$accident_class,
  prop_train = 0.60,
  prop_val = 0.20,
  seed = 2026
)

train_svm <- atus_svm[parts_atus$train, ]
val_svm <- atus_svm[parts_atus$validation, ]
test_svm <- atus_svm[parts_atus$test, ]

rbind(
  training = prop.table(table(train_svm$accident_class)),
  validation = prop.table(table(val_svm$accident_class)),
  test = prop.table(table(test_svm$accident_class))
)
```

## Class weights

When classes are imbalanced, `class.weights = "inverse"` assigns weights inversely proportional to the class frequencies in the data used to fit each model.

::: {.callout-note title="What class weights do—and do not do"}
Weights modify the cost of training errors. They do not replace evaluation with sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy.
:::

## Joint selection of kernel, `cost`, and `gamma`

The test set is not involved in this search. Seven configurations are compared on the **validation set**.

```{r svm-grid-atus-en}
svm_grid <- bind_rows(
  data.frame(
    kernel = "linear",
    cost = c(0.25, 1, 4),
    gamma = NA_real_
  ),
  expand.grid(
    kernel = "radial",
    cost = c(0.5, 2),
    gamma = c(0.01, 0.05),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
)

svm_formula <- accident_class ~
  MES + HOUR_NUM + DIASEMANA + TIPACCID + CAUSAACCI
```

```{r svm-validate-grid-atus-en}
svm_validation_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(svm_grid)), function(i) {
    cfg <- svm_grid[i, ]

    set.seed(2026 + i)

    model <- if (cfg$kernel == "linear") {
      svm(
        svm_formula,
        data = train_svm,
        kernel = "linear",
        cost = cfg$cost,
        class.weights = "inverse",
        scale = TRUE
      )
    } else {
      svm(
        svm_formula,
        data = train_svm,
        kernel = "radial",
        cost = cfg$cost,
        gamma = cfg$gamma,
        class.weights = "inverse",
        scale = TRUE
      )
    }

    pred <- predict(model, newdata = val_svm)

    m <- svm_metrics(
      val_svm$accident_class,
      pred,
      positive = "With casualties",
      negative = "Property damage only"
    )$metrics

    cbind(
      cfg,
      support_vectors = model$tot.nSV,
      m
    )
  })
)

svm_validation_results
```

## Choose the configuration

```{r svm-select-best-atus-en}
best_row <- which.max(svm_validation_results$balanced_accuracy)
best_config <- svm_validation_results[best_row, ]

best_config
```

```{r svm-validation-plot-atus-en, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5}
svm_validation_results <- svm_validation_results |>
  mutate(
    configuration = ifelse(
      kernel == "linear",
      paste0("linear C=", cost),
      paste0("radial C=", cost, ", gamma=", gamma)
    )
  )

svm_validation_long <- svm_validation_results |>
  select(
    configuration,
    sensitivity,
    specificity,
    balanced_accuracy
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -configuration,
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "value"
  )

ggplot(
  svm_validation_long,
  aes(x = configuration, y = value, fill = metric)
) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "SVM selection on the validation set",
    subtitle = "The test set remains untouched",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Metric",
    fill = "Metric"
  ) +
  tema_libro()
```

## Refit with training + validation data

```{r svm-refit-final-atus-en}
reference_svm <- bind_rows(train_svm, val_svm)

if (best_config$kernel == "linear") {
  final_svm <- svm(
    svm_formula,
    data = reference_svm,
    kernel = "linear",
    cost = best_config$cost,
    class.weights = "inverse",
    scale = TRUE
  )
} else {
  final_svm <- svm(
    svm_formula,
    data = reference_svm,
    kernel = "radial",
    cost = best_config$cost,
    gamma = best_config$gamma,
    class.weights = "inverse",
    scale = TRUE
  )
}

final_svm$tot.nSV
```

## One-time final test evaluation

```{r svm-final-evaluation-atus-en}
pred_svm_test <- predict(
  final_svm,
  newdata = test_svm
)

result_svm_test <- svm_metrics(
  test_svm$accident_class,
  pred_svm_test,
  positive = "With casualties",
  negative = "Property damage only"
)

result_svm_test$confusion
result_svm_test$metrics
```

::: {.callout-important title="Correct interpretation"}
The configuration was selected using validation data and the test set was used once. If `cost`, `gamma`, kernel, class weights, or predictors are changed after inspecting test results, that test set is no longer an independent estimate of final performance.
:::

## Support vectors and model complexity

The number of support vectors describes how much of the reference set directly participates in the decision boundary. It is not, by itself, a quality metric: two SVMs can use different numbers of support vectors and have similar predictive performance.

# Interactive laboratory: margin and hyperplane

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
Explore a linear boundary of the form $w_1x_1+w_2x_2+b=0$, its margins, and the classification of a new point.

```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 720
#| components: [viewer]

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  titlePanel("Interactive linear SVM explorer"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      sliderInput("w1", "Weight w1", -3, 3, 1, step = 0.1),
      sliderInput("w2", "Weight w2", -3, 3, -1, step = 0.1),
      sliderInput("b", "Bias b", -3, 3, 0, step = 0.1),
      sliderInput("x1", "New point: x1", -4, 4, 1, step = 0.1),
      sliderInput("x2", "New point: x2", -4, 4, 1, step = 0.1)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("plane", height = "440px"),
      verbatimTextOutput("result"),
      textOutput("interpretation")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  decision_value <- reactive({
    input$w1 * input$x1 + input$w2 * input$x2 + input$b
  })

  output$plane <- renderPlot({
    plot(
      NA,
      xlim = c(-4, 4),
      ylim = c(-4, 4),
      xlab = "x1",
      ylab = "x2",
      main = "Hyperplane and margins"
    )
    grid()

    if (abs(input$w2) > 1e-8) {
      abline(a = -input$b / input$w2,
             b = -input$w1 / input$w2,
             lwd = 3)
      abline(a = -(input$b - 1) / input$w2,
             b = -input$w1 / input$w2,
             lty = 2)
      abline(a = -(input$b + 1) / input$w2,
             b = -input$w1 / input$w2,
             lty = 2)
    } else if (abs(input$w1) > 1e-8) {
      abline(v = -input$b / input$w1, lwd = 3)
      abline(v = -(input$b - 1) / input$w1, lty = 2)
      abline(v = -(input$b + 1) / input$w1, lty = 2)
    }

    points(input$x1, input$x2, pch = 19, cex = 2)
  })

  output$result <- renderPrint({
    cat("Decision value:", round(decision_value(), 4), "\n")
    cat("Predicted class:", ifelse(decision_value() >= 0, "Class +1", "Class -1"))
  })

  output$interpretation <- renderText({
    paste0(
      "The sign of the decision value determines the class. ",
      "Functional margins are shown with dashed lines."
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
:::

# Applied Case B: SVM with COVID-19

## Select the same reproducible period

```{r covid-svm-period-en}
covid_counts <- read_csv(
  "../datos/covid19/procesados/conteo_casos_confirmados_2020_2025.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

covid_year <- covid_counts |>
  filter(ESTADO == "PROCESADO", !is.na(CASOS_CONFIRMADOS)) |>
  slice_max(CASOS_CONFIRMADOS, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  pull(ANIO)

covid_path <- file.path(
  "../datos/covid19/procesados",
  paste0("covid19_mexico_", covid_year, "_ml_preparado.csv.gz")
)

if (!file.exists(covid_path)) {
  stop("The COVID-19 dataset selected by the reproducible procedure was not found.")
}
```

## Prepare and split the sample

```{r covid-svm-prepare-en}
covid_svm <- read_csv(covid_path, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  select(
    MURIO, EDAD, NEUMONIA, DIABETES, HIPERTENSION,
    OBESIDAD, RENAL_CRONICA, NUM_COMORBILIDADES
  ) |>
  drop_na() |>
  mutate(
    outcome = factor(
      MURIO,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("No recorded death", "Recorded death")
    )
  ) |>
  select(-MURIO)

set.seed(2026)
covid_svm <- covid_svm |>
  slice_sample(n = min(6000, n()))

parts_covid <- stratified_svm_split(
  covid_svm$outcome,
  prop_train = 0.60,
  prop_val = 0.20,
  seed = 2026
)

covid_train <- covid_svm[parts_covid$train, ]
covid_val <- covid_svm[parts_covid$validation, ]
covid_test <- covid_svm[parts_covid$test, ]
```

::: {.callout-warning title="Educational use only"}
This exercise illustrates SVM behavior on administrative data. It is not a clinical, diagnostic, or prognostic tool. If sampling changes prevalence, its outputs should not be interpreted as population risk.
:::

## Select a configuration with validation

To control computation time, the COVID-19 route uses a smaller grid.

```{r covid-svm-validation-en}
covid_svm_formula <- outcome ~
  EDAD + NEUMONIA + DIABETES + HIPERTENSION +
  OBESIDAD + RENAL_CRONICA + NUM_COMORBILIDADES

covid_grid <- data.frame(
  kernel = c("linear", "radial", "radial"),
  cost = c(1, 1, 2),
  gamma = c(NA, 1 / 7, 0.05)
)

covid_svm_results <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_len(nrow(covid_grid)), function(i) {
    cfg <- covid_grid[i, ]

    model <- if (cfg$kernel == "linear") {
      svm(
        covid_svm_formula,
        data = covid_train,
        kernel = "linear",
        cost = cfg$cost,
        class.weights = "inverse",
        scale = TRUE
      )
    } else {
      svm(
        covid_svm_formula,
        data = covid_train,
        kernel = "radial",
        cost = cfg$cost,
        gamma = cfg$gamma,
        class.weights = "inverse",
        scale = TRUE
      )
    }

    pred <- predict(model, covid_val)
    m <- svm_metrics(
      covid_val$outcome,
      pred,
      positive = "Recorded death",
      negative = "No recorded death"
    )$metrics

    cbind(cfg, support_vectors = model$tot.nSV, m)
  })
)

covid_svm_results
```

## Final COVID-19 evaluation

```{r covid-svm-final-en}
best_covid <- covid_svm_results[
  which.max(covid_svm_results$balanced_accuracy),
]

covid_reference <- bind_rows(covid_train, covid_val)

final_covid_svm <- if (best_covid$kernel == "linear") {
  svm(
    covid_svm_formula,
    data = covid_reference,
    kernel = "linear",
    cost = best_covid$cost,
    class.weights = "inverse",
    scale = TRUE
  )
} else {
  svm(
    covid_svm_formula,
    data = covid_reference,
    kernel = "radial",
    cost = best_covid$cost,
    gamma = best_covid$gamma,
    class.weights = "inverse",
    scale = TRUE
  )
}

pred_covid_final <- predict(final_covid_svm, covid_test)

result_covid_final <- svm_metrics(
  covid_test$outcome,
  pred_covid_final,
  positive = "Recorded death",
  negative = "No recorded death"
)

result_covid_final$confusion
result_covid_final$metrics
```

## Advantages and limitations

### Advantages

- can model linear and nonlinear boundaries;
- can work well in high-dimensional spaces;
- margin maximization provides a clear geometric regularization principle;
- supports class weighting;
- the solution depends directly on support vectors.

### Limitations

- can be computationally expensive on large datasets;
- requires kernel and hyperparameter selection;
- is less interpretable than logistic regression or a small tree;
- is sensitive to numeric predictor scale;
- extensive hyperparameter searches can be expensive.

## Activities for the reader

1. Expand the `cost` and `gamma` grid while keeping the test set untouched.
2. Select the configuration by maximizing sensitivity instead of balanced accuracy.
3. Compare SVMs with and without class weights.
4. Record the number of support vectors for each configuration and discuss whether it is directly related to performance.
5. Compare the final SVM with logistic regression and Random Forest using the same split.

## Chapter summary

SVMs combine a powerful geometric idea—the margin—with kernels capable of constructing nonlinear boundaries. Reliable use requires control of scaling, imbalance, and hyperparameters. Kernel, `cost`, and `gamma` should be selected using training/validation information, and the final test set should be used once to estimate generalization.

## Fundamental references

SVMs were formalized by @cortes1995support. The tutorial by @burges1998tutorial develops margins and kernels. An applied introduction can be found in @james2021islr.
